text:
Dylan Garand did the quiet, decisive work at Little Caesars Arena, stopping all 22 shots he faced for the Rangers in a 2-0 win over Detroit that was far closer than the scoreboard suggests. At even strength the two teams were level in chance quality (1.37 expected goals for NYR, 1.36 for DET), and Detroit actually had the better of the opening period, 1.03 to 0.73. Garand's 1.70 goals saved above expected came from a Red Wings team that kept generating real looks, and he turned all of them away.

New York took the lead on its one early power play. Sean Durzi's slap shot at 5:12 of the first, set up by Gabe Perreault and Will Cuylle, carried only an 8 percent chance of scoring, which is the kind of goal a team gets by shooting through traffic and hoping. John Gibson was good at the other end, 1.12 goals above expected on 20 shots, and kept Detroit within a single goal for nearly the whole night. The Rangers' 3.02 total expected goals, nearly double Detroit's 1.70, leans heavily on special teams and a late push, not on sustained control.

The third period is where the gap opened. New York out-chanced Detroit 1.45 to 0.08 in the final 20 minutes, and Eeli Tolvanen finished a 57 percent chance with a wrist shot at 18:44, assisted by Tye Kartye and Adam Fox, to put it away. By the simulated replays, the Rangers deserved the win 58 percent of the time. Detroit's 42 percent says this was no robbery, but for 40 minutes it could have gone either way.
